Topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

Target audience: University students (Linear Algebra introductory course)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Warm-up: The Transformation Perspective

Lecture lines:
Matrices act as functions moving the entire coordinate plane.
A matrix A transforms a vector v into w.
Think of this as a transformation of the grid.

Planned animations:


Section: section_2 — The Concept of Function Composition

Lecture lines:
Composition means applying one transformation after another.
We apply B first, then A to result C.
We want a single matrix C for AB.
Robotic arm rotates then extends its reach.
This sequence equals a combined transformation matrix.

Planned animations:


Section: section_3 — Visualizing the Chain Reaction

Lecture lines:
Track the basis vectors i and j.
B moves basis vectors to new positions.
A then moves those results again.
Final positions define the columns of matrix C.
This chain is the matrix product AB.

Planned animations:


Section: section_4 — Deriving the Rule: Why 'Row by Column'?

Lecture lines:
Matrix multiplication is not commutative, so AB does not equal BA.
It tracks where basis vectors end up after two mappings.
Scaling then flipping differs from flipping then scaling.

Planned animations:


Section: section_5 — Summary and Conclusion

Lecture lines:
Matrix multiplication is a geometric shortcut.
Multiply matrices once to capture the full movement.
Compute a single matrix for efficient composite transformations.

        # BASE

        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        return mobject

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
